description: Hand-drawn pixel typeface: one strike per size, with CSS that keeps type, spacing, and borders on the same pixel grid.
rules: Prefer the Tailwind happy path: `@import "quanta-strike/base-12.css"` (or another base-N). That loads fonts, type scale, pixel grid, and zoom together.
Size and family are a pair. Use each strike only at its native size (font-size = N px). Never change font-size without also changing the matching font-family / strike class.
Do not mix locked `.qs-N` classes with a `base-N` preset or `--qs-zoom`. `.qs-N` ignores zoom and puts a second pixel size on the page.
Prefer integer `--qs-zoom` for sharp pixels on every display. `1.5` is fine on retina; avoid awkward fractions like `1.75`.
For plain CSS without the scale system, import `quanta-strike` and use `.qs-N` / `.qs-N-mono` classes.
Mono is a separate family, not a weight of proportional. Use `base-N-mono`, `mono.css`, or `.qs-mono` on a subtree — not `font-family: …-mono` alone without the matching size.
Responsive type: do not use clamp() across strikes. Swap the whole size+family pair at a breakpoint, or change `--qs-zoom` to scale every strike together.
Avoid the `text-decoration` shorthand — it resets thickness to `auto`. Use `text-decoration-line` and let grid.css / strike classes set thickness.
